profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company founded in 1993, headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and traded as NVDA. For the fiscal period ended January 25, 2026, it reported revenue of $215,938,000,000 in a 10-K filing. NVIDIA has 281 California legal exposure entries.

The company's AI products include NVIDIA Nemotron, described as an enterprise LLM family with synthetic data generation, GPU optimization, and self-hosted options, and NVIDIA NIM, inference microservices for deploying foundation models with enterprise GPU optimization and self-hosted options. NVIDIA's website describes the Nemotron family as highly efficient, multimodal, open AI models built for long-running, self-evolving agents, with transparent training data and support for NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark. The page says Nemotron 3.5 Lightning helps agents complete specialized tasks faster, while NeMo Switchyard routes each step to the right model. Nemotron models are available as NVIDIA NIM microservices, which require an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license, and NVIDIA publishes training datasets, techniques, and model weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License.

The page also mentions Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, discussing the vision behind Nemotron, and cites ServiceNow's evaluation of visual Q&A accuracy. NVIDIA says it works with partners across the ecosystem, including model builders and AI-native companies, to improve Nemotron models through shared expertise, data, evaluation, and real-world feedback.
